text: /// The canonical ids of the `plugins` an applicable `use` entry names, which
/// is what wakes a dormant one. A plugin is named by its manifest name, under
/// the rule of the package manager it came from.
/// A registry compares plugin names exactly, so only the exact spelling
/// in `use` wakes a dormant registry plugin.
.expect_err("a registry plugin name is not a crate name");
/// A registry plugin's name matches exactly: `use = ["gateless_plugin"]`
/// neither wakes the dormant `gateless-plugin` nor is taken for a crate, and
/// `disable = ["gateless_plugin"]` does not block it. `auto-enable` is consent
/// for dependencies, so it wakes no registry plugin whatever the spelling.

rationale:
Registry instances (`PathPm`, `GitPm`) use the default `PackageManager::canonical_name` (`symposium-sdk/src/pm.rs`: returns the name unchanged), and `PmRegistry::identity` falls back to the name as-is for unknown owners. Hence:

- `used_plugins` builds `PackageId::any_version(p.canonical.pm, p.manifest.name)` and checks `is_used_in` -> `name_matches` -> exact comparison for registry plugins.
- `PmRegistry::identify` (used by `resolve_used` and `cargo agents use`) matches a registry plugin by `identity` under the registry pm: exact.
- `is_disabled` against a registry id is exact too.

Tests (all pass): `discovery::tests::use_wakes_a_registry_plugin_only_by_its_exact_name` (`my-plugin` wakes, `my_plugin` does not); `tests/enablement.rs` `use_matches_registry_plugin_names_exactly` (`use gateless_plugin` errors "no package named"), `plugins_entries_match_registry_plugin_names_exactly` (folded `use` spelling does not wake; folded `disable` spelling does not block; exact `disable` does).

**Refuted on review:** the comparison is exact only in the common case. (1) `PmRegistry::identity` (src/pm/mod.rs) picks the canonicalizing package manager by `owner(id)`, the first instance whose name equals `id.pm`, and the cargo transport is always pushed first (src/config.rs `package_managers`). Nothing reserves the registry name `cargo` (`registry_instance` accepts any name), so for `[[registry]] name = "cargo"` every plugin from that registry is canonicalized with `CargoPm::canonical_name`, which folds `-`/`_`. Reproduced with the prebuilt binary: registry `cargo` holding dormant `my-plugin` and `[plugins] use = ["my_plugin"]` makes `cargo agents status` report "my-plugin — `[plugins] use`" as active; renaming the registry to `reg` leaves it dormant and lists `my_plugin` as unresolved. The same folding applies to `disable` and `cargo agents use`. (2) `name_matches` (src/config.rs) begins with `entry == "*" ||`, and it backs `is_used_in` and `is_disabled`, so a `[plugins] use = ["*"]` entry wakes every dormant registry plugin whatever its name (status shows `my-plugin` active via `[plugins] use` while also listing `*` as matching nothing), and `disable = ["*"]` matches every registry plugin (e.g. `cargo agents use my-plugin` is rejected at src/use_command.rs:51-56). `"*"` is documented only for `auto-enable`, so a `[plugins]` name other than the plugin's own name matching it is not an exact comparison. The rationale's "exact comparison for registry plugins" claim omits both branches.
requirement: Symposium MUST compare a `[plugins]` or `cargo agents use` name with a registry plugin's name exactly.
